title: Learned Sparse Retrieval: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Learned Sparse Retrieval: Visual Guide

1. One Index, Not Two | three architectures tapped side by side - BM25 alone, the Atrium Pattern (BM25 + vectors + RRF + reranker), and learned sparse - each with its parts list, storage-system and fusion-step counters, and how it answers an exact-match query versus 'heart attack symptoms' | the fused stack covers both failure modes by running two systems, while learned sparse covers both inside one inverted index, in the same engine, cluster and runbook the team already operates

2. The Sparsity Dial | a slider on the FLOPS-style regulariser, showing the weights of the query 'heart attack symptoms' - in-text terms, expansions (cardiac, chest, myocardial) and a wrong-sense activation - collapsing to zero, with the active-term count out of ~30,000 and posting lists to walk | SPLADE's pipeline is MLM head over 30k terms, log(1+ReLU(x)), max-pool, and the sparsity regulariser is an explicit dial chosen at training time and paid as serving latency, with a workable operating point of a few dozen to a couple of hundred active terms

3. Two Ways To Expand | a doc2query-versus-SPLADE comparison table over five rows (where expansion happens, mechanism, scoring, query side, stack change) plus doc2query's own dial for predicted queries appended per document, computing offline inferences over a 1,000,000-document corpus | doc2query expands the document text at index time and keeps plain BM25 for zero serving-stack change but 10 million inferences and a much larger index, while SPLADE expands at encode time, expands the query too, and scores with contextual learned weights

4. Impact-Sorted Postings | one term's 12-document posting list flipped between docID order and descending impact weight, with a top-k slider counting postings actually examined, and an 8-bit versus 16-bit quantisation toggle changing levels, stored bytes and displayed precision | impact sorting trades merge intersection for early termination that returns the identical top-k after examining only k postings, quantised weights make the WAND/MaxScore bounds exact rather than estimated, and everything else about the index survives unchanged

5. Shipped Learned Sparse | three shipped configurations (Elastic ELSER, OpenSearch neural sparse document-only encoding, OpenSearch neural sparse bi-encoder mode) broken down by doc side, query side, field, scoring and catch, plus seven tappable constraints that each argue for learned sparse or for dense | learned sparse ships in mainstream engines as an ordinary rank_features field scored by the same engine that runs BM25, and the choice against dense is decided by constraints - traffic mix, infrastructure family, CPU-only serving, explainability, corpus language and document length - not by a benchmark number
